S58.01.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access (tier-dependent) and at least one connector or custom MCP server added
S58.01.note: The quoted Code lines moved; the list is rendered in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx (ConnectorCard and the filtered rows). The Settings entry control (how the tester first opens Settings) was not confirmed; the path above starts at the Settings screen. Listing is per signed-in account; I found no workspace-level list.
steps: Open Settings and tap Cloud, then tap Connectors.
Wait for the connector list to load (a loading label may show first).
Look at the filter chips (All, Connected, Custom) and the connector rows; each row shows a status such as Connected or Not connected.
Compare with Expected: your configured MCP servers (custom ones show under the Custom filter) should appear in this list.

labels.text: Add a remote MCP server by its HTTPS URL to use its tools in chat.

S58.03.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access, and a remote MCP server HTTPS URL to test with
S58.03.note: The URL must be HTTPS (the modal shows a reason line for a non-HTTPS URL). The Add button text is just Add; the sheet's accessibility label is Add connector.
steps: Open Settings, tap Cloud, then tap Connectors.
Scroll to the bottom of the list and tap Add custom MCP.
In the Add custom MCP connector sheet, type a Name, type an https:// Connector URL, and optionally an Auth token, then tap Add.

Look for the new server in the connector list (filter Custom) with a status; compare with Expected. Tool use in chat is at the + sheet under Connectors (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx), not confirmed on device.
S58.03.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Add custom MCP

S58.06.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access, and a valid token or API key or an outside account to sign in to
S58.06.note: Secure storage is server-side: the custom connector's description reads Your encrypted remote MCP endpoint (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx). I did not confirm the on-device storage mechanism. The Connect button is shown only for listings not yet connected, so its exact condition was not traced.
steps: For a custom server: open Settings, tap Cloud, tap Connectors, tap Add custom MCP.
Type the URL and fill the Auth token (optional) field; the field hides the text as you type.
Tap Add, then open the new server and check that it shows as connected.

For a listed connector: open it from the Connectors list and tap Connect. For an API-key connector, enter the key in the sheet and tap Test and save; for an account sign-in connector, follow the sign-in step that opens. Compare with Expected: the token or key is accepted and the connector shows as connected, with no key shown back.
S58.06.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Add custom MCP (Auth token field); for a listed connector, Settings > Cloud > Connectors > [connector name] > Connect

S58.08.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access and a connected MCP server or connector
S58.08.note: Tool names are read from the catalog only after the connector is connected; an unconnected listing shows a note that it lists tools once connected.
steps: Open Settings, tap Cloud, tap Connectors, and tap a connector that is Connected.
Scroll down to the Tool permissions heading.
Wait for Loading tools to finish; if it fails, tap Retry loading tools.
Look at the groups Read-only tools and Write and delete tools and the tool names under them. Compare with Expected: the connector's tools are listed.
S58.08.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > [a connected connector] > Tool permissions

S58.12.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Connectors access, a connected connector, and ideally a few tool calls made in chat first
S58.12.note: The Recent calls copy says it shows what the connector was asked to do, without arguments or results. I did not confirm the empty-state text shown before any calls exist.
steps: Open Settings, tap Cloud, tap Connectors, and tap a connected connector.
Scroll to the Connection health card and read its state and summary line.
Tap Check again to refresh the health reading.
Scroll to the Recent calls section and read the rows (outcomes Worked, Failed or Blocked here). Compare with Expected: health and recent call history are visible for this server.
S58.12.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > [a connected connector] > Connection health (then Recent calls below it)
